quotes/hagin-positive-confession/text: Hagin taught that believers, by speaking in faith what God has promised in Scripture, can appropriate healing and material provision that are already theirs through Christ’s redemption; doubt and negative confession block the blessing.
quotes/tertullian-soul-propagated/text: Tertullian holds that the soul comes into being together with the body at conception and is propagated from the parents’ souls, as a shoot from a root, so that every soul is “in Adam” and shares his fault until it is renewed in Christ.
quotes/tertullian-devils-gateway/text: And do you not know that you are (each) an Eve? The sentence of God on this sex of yours lives in this age: the guilt must of necessity live too. You are the devil’s gateway.
quotes/origen-preexistent-souls/text: Origen speculates that all rational beings were created equal and pre-existent, and that the diversity of their present conditions — angels, humans, demons — results from the different degrees of their falling away from God.
quotes/nyssa-whole-humanity-image/text: Gregory teaches that the image of God belongs not to one part of human nature or to one individual but to the whole of humanity, from first to last, which God foresaw as a single whole; the image consists above all in freedom, reason and the capacity for virtue.
quotes/chrysostom-romans-sinners/text: Commenting on “by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners” (Romans 5:19), Chrysostom suggests that “sinners” here means those liable to punishment and condemned to death, since it would be unreasonable for one to be a sinner through another’s disobedience.
quotes/augustine-soul-origin-uncertain/t: Augustine confesses to Jerome that he cannot decide whether new souls are created individually by God or derived from the parents; he must hold, however, that infants share Adam’s condemnation, and he begs Jerome to show how the creation of souls is compatible with that.
quotes/aquinas-image-in-mind/text: Aquinas teaches that the image of God is found properly in the rational mind, by which humans can know and love God; it exists naturally in all, by grace in the just and by glory in the blessed.
quotes/aquinas-woman-misbegotten/text: As regards the individual nature, woman is defective and misbegotten.
quotes/erasmus-free-will-para/text: Erasmus defines free will as a power by which a person can apply himself to the things that lead to salvation or turn away from them; he argues that commands and exhortations throughout Scripture would be pointless if humans could contribute nothing.
quotes/zwingli-original-disease/text: Zwingli describes original sin as a disease or defect inherited from Adam — a bent toward self-love — rather than a sin in the proper sense, which requires transgression of a law; it nonetheless leads to sin and death unless healed by Christ.
quotes/articles-original-sin/text: Original Sin standeth not in the following of Adam, (as the Pelagians do vainly talk;) but it is the fault and corruption of the Nature of every man, that naturally is engendered of the offspring of Adam; whereby man is very far gone from original righteousness.
quotes/flacius-sin-substance/text: Flacius argues that after the fall original sin is not an accident clinging to human nature but the formal substance of the fallen person: the image of God has been transformed into the image of Satan.
quotes/wesley-no-mere-nature/text: For allowing that all the souls of men are dead in sin by nature, this excuses none, seeing there is no man that is in a state of mere nature; there is no man, unless he has quenched the Spirit, that is wholly void of the grace of God.
quotes/edwards-freedom-para/text: Edwards argues that the will is always as the greatest apparent good is; a person is free when able to do what he wills, and the moral necessity by which a heart chooses according to its strongest inclination is fully compatible with praise and blame.
quotes/edwards-constituted-one/text: Edwards argues that God, who upholds every created thing in being from moment to moment, may justly constitute Adam and his posterity as one, so that their sharing in his first sin is no more arbitrary than the identity of any person through time.
quotes/nee-tripartite/text: Nee teaches that the human being has three parts: the spirit, which knows God; the soul (mind, emotion and will), which is the seat of personality; and the body. The fall reversed their right order, and the spiritual life means the spirit ruling the soul and body.
quotes/barth-image-relational/text: Barth interprets the image of God not as a quality humans possess but as a relation: humanity exists in encounter and partnership, above all as male and female, mirroring the I-Thou relation within God and God’s covenant with humanity.
quotes/romanides-ancestral-para/text: Romanides argues that for the Greek Fathers humans inherit from Adam not guilt but death and corruption; the fear of death enslaves humans to selfishness and sin, and Christ saves by destroying death and the devil.
quotes/saiving-pride-para/text: Saiving suggests that the specifically feminine forms of sin are better described as triviality, distractibility, diffuseness, dependence on others for self-definition — in short, underdevelopment or negation of the self — rather than pride and will-to-power.
quotes/cone-racism-sin-para/text: Cone argues that white racism is a fundamental sin of American Christianity, and that because God in the Exodus and in Jesus sides with the oppressed, Christian theology must speak from the experience of Black people struggling for liberation.
quotes/murphy-physicalism-para/text: Murphy argues that neuroscience shows capacities once attributed to the soul to be functions of the brain, and that Christians lose nothing essential by abandoning body-soul dualism: the biblical hope is for resurrection of the whole person, not escape of a soul.
quotes/hodge-imputation/text: Hodge teaches that as Adam’s sin is imputed to his posterity by virtue of the covenant in which he stood as their federal head, so Christ’s righteousness — his obedience and his satisfaction of justice — is imputed to believers as the sole ground of their justification, which is a forensic declaration, not an inward change.
quotes/piper-imputation/text: Piper argues that the imputation of Christ’s perfect righteousness to the believer is essential to the gospel: God counts us righteous in Christ not because of any transformation in us, and this alone gives a sure footing for assurance and joy before a holy God.
quotes/tf-torrance-latin-heresy/text: T. F. Torrance criticises what he calls the "Latin heresy": a habit of thinking of Christ’s relation to sinners in external, legal terms, so that atonement becomes a transaction outside the person of the Mediator rather than reconciliation worked out within his incarnate humanity.
quotes/jb-torrance-covenant-contract/tex: J. B. Torrance contrasts covenant with contract: in a covenant God freely commits himself in love and then calls for a response of gratitude, whereas federal theology’s "covenant of works" turned grace into a conditional contract, so that the indicatives of grace were made dependent on the imperatives of law.
quotes/jb-torrance-worship/text: J. B. Torrance describes Christian worship as the gift of participating through the Spirit in the incarnate Son’s own communion with the Father, rather than a human work offered to God to secure his favour.
quotes/barth-election-in-christ/text: Barth teaches that Jesus Christ is both the electing God and the elected man: in him God has chosen humanity for fellowship with himself and has taken the rejection due to sinners upon himself, so that election is the sum of the gospel. He declined either to affirm or to deny universal salvation as a doctrine.
quotes/kruger-included/text: Kruger argues that the Father, Son and Spirit share a life of fellowship and joy, and that in becoming human the Son has included the whole human race in that life; the gospel announces what is already true in Jesus and invites people to believe and live it, rather than to make it true by their decision.
quotes/du-toit-mirror/text: Du Toit teaches that Scripture is a mirror revealing humanity’s original identity in Christ: in Jesus’ death and resurrection all humanity was co-crucified and co-raised (2 Corinthians 5:14; Ephesians 2:5-6), so that faith is awakening to and agreeing with what God has already accomplished, not a condition that completes it.
quotes/packer-legal-framework/text: Packer argues that God’s relation to humanity is rightly described in legal terms because God is Judge as well as Father; justification is God’s judicial verdict of acquittal grounded on Christ’s substitutionary satisfaction, and without it adoption and assurance have no foundation.
quotes/irenaeus-eve-mary/text: And thus also it was that the knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary. For what the virgin Eve had bound fast through unbelief, this did the virgin Mary set free through faith.
quotes/basil-image-prototype/text: …because the honour paid to the image passes on to the prototype.
quotes/ephrem-mary-no-stain/text: Ephrem sings that Christ and his mother alone are wholly beautiful: in the Lord there is no blemish, and in his Mother no stain.
quotes/jerome-against-helvidius-virgin/t: Jerome argues that the ‘brethren of the Lord’ were his kinsmen — the sons of Mary's sister — and that Mary, and Joseph too, remained virgins, so that the Lord was born of a virgin marriage.
quotes/augustine-mary-no-sin/text: We must except the holy Virgin Mary, concerning whom I wish to raise no question when it touches the subject of sins, out of honour to the Lord; for from Him we know what abundance of grace for overcoming sin in every particular was conferred upon her who had the merit to conceive and bear Him who undoubtedly had no sin.
quotes/john-damascus-matter/text: I do not worship matter, I worship the Creator of matter, who became matter for my sake, who willed to take His abode in matter, who worked out my salvation through matter.
quotes/john-damascus-worship-veneration/: John of Damascus distinguishes worship (latreia), owed to God alone, from the relative honour or veneration (proskynesis) given to holy persons, places and images for God's sake.
quotes/aquinas-mary-sanctified/text: Aquinas holds that Mary was sanctified in her mother's womb after her animation, not before, since otherwise she would not have needed redemption by Christ, who is the Saviour of all.
quotes/scotus-preservative-redemption/te: Scotus argues that a most perfect mediator must have a most perfect act of mediation for at least one person; it is more perfect to preserve someone from original sin than to free them from it afterward, so it is fitting that Christ did this for his mother.
quotes/luther-magnificat-regard/text: Luther writes that Mary is to be honoured not for her own merit but because God regarded her lowliness; she does not want us to come to her, but through her to God, and those who heap glory on her detract from the grace of God.
quotes/pius-ix-immaculate/text: …the most Blessed Virgin Mary, in the first instance of her conception, by a singular grace and privilege granted by Almighty God, in view of the merits of Jesus Christ, the Savior of the human race, was preserved free from all stain of original sin.
